name: autopilot-console-phase-1
description: Build the Phase 1 self-hosted Autopilot Console control plane from project registration through durable Autopilot execution and GitHub feature-PR merge detection.
goals: Provide a mobile-friendly global portfolio overview and a complete Needs Your Attention queue for up to 10 projects.
Model projects, releases, features, approved task artifacts, immutable job attempts, pull requests, activity, and audit history in PostgreSQL.
Validate and approve existing project-relative autopilot task JSON, then atomically queue durable background development.
Run up to four jobs across different projects while enforcing one active job per project and preserving work across browser or API disconnects.
Expose requirement-level TDD progress from structured task files, notes, analytics, and Git history through an AutopilotRunner boundary.
Push one deterministic feature branch, create one GitHub PR, poll current-head CI and review state, and detect external merge without merging from Console.
Make every human and automated transition secure, idempotent, auditable, accessible, and reconstructable from persisted state.
nonGoals: Reimplementing or forking the autopilot-multi TDD engine.
Generating or editing PRDs or task JSON in the web application.
Launching agent repair jobs for development, CI, review, test, or deployment failures.
DEV, UAT, GitHub Release, production deployment, or production-readiness workflows.
Automatically approving or merging feature pull requests.
Cloning repositories, destructive workspace reset, arbitrary checkout management, or multiple worktrees per project.
Multi-user access, RBAC, SSO, tenant isolation, or non-GitHub source-control providers.
GitHub webhooks or outbound email, SMS, chat, or push notifications.
Same-project concurrent development, sprint planning, native mobile applications, or offline mutations.
technicalNotes: Requirements 1-20 establish the domain, persistence, adapter, queue, process-control, and GitHub worker components. Requirements 21-48 distinguish component behavior, production composition, owner UI, and release qualification so one missing deployment or test gate does not obscure otherwise complete work. A requirement passes only when every acceptance statement is directly exercised by its named test and every verification step succeeds; a component-level test does not prove that the component is composed in apps/api/src/main.ts, apps/worker/src/main.ts, or compose.yaml. PostgreSQL remains the source of truth. Long-running, process, Git, and GitHub effects belong to durable worker consumers, never HTTP request scope. Use isolated database schemas, controllable executables/adapters, fake clocks or bounded event synchronization, fixed argv without a shell, redaction before persistence/emission, UTC at rest, and at least 90% branch coverage for every named critical module.
_priority_order: 1. Bootstrap executable workspace and test infrastructure
2. Establish persistence, domain invariants, security, and external adapter contracts
3. Implement durable queue, worker, process, Git, and GitHub orchestration
4. Expose authenticated APIs and persisted read models
5. Build responsive owner workflows and accessibility behavior
6. Prove deployment, end-to-end durability, performance, and quality gates
_step_size: Complete one requirement through Red, Green, and Refactor before starting a dependent requirement; make one logical change per commit and never commit failing tests, typecheck, or lint.

requirements.description: Bootstrap the Bun workspace, package boundaries, TypeScript configuration, and executable test, lint, typecheck, coverage, and build quality gates.

patterns: The PRD prescribes a Bun workspace with separate web, API, worker, database, domain, shared, Autopilot, GitHub, and Git packages.
No existing package manager, application code, test framework, lint configuration, or TypeScript configuration exists.

acceptance: The root workspace discovers all three apps and all six prescribed packages with unambiguous package names and dependency boundaries.
Root scripts run tests, typecheck, lint, coverage, and production builds across the workspace and return nonzero on any package failure.
Coverage configuration can enforce branch thresholds for selected critical packages without counting generated migrations or fixtures.
TypeScript strict mode and consistent module-resolution settings apply to every workspace package.
The architecture test fails before workspace configuration exists and passes only when all required boundaries and quality scripts are present.
No empty source module, stub function, skipped test, or placeholder implementation is introduced during bootstrap.

test.description: Create tests/architecture/workspace.test.ts first to assert the package graph, strict compiler inheritance, required root scripts, and critical coverage configuration; run it directly with Bun and verify the missing workspace fails.

implement.description: Add the minimal Bun workspace manifests, lockfile, strict TypeScript base configuration, Biome rules, Bun test/coverage configuration, and package manifests needed to satisfy the architecture test.

refactor.description: Remove duplicated package scripts through root conventions where practical, verify package dependency directions remain explicit, then run install, test, typecheck, lint, coverage, and build gates.

verification: Run bun install --frozen-lockfile.
Run bun run test, bun run typecheck, bun run lint, bun run coverage, and bun run build.
Inspect workspace resolution and confirm apps do not import another app directly.

requirements.description: Create shared runtime configuration, API contracts, identifiers, idempotency primitives, normalized errors, correlation metadata, and secret redaction.

patterns: The PRD requires documented API contracts, stable operation keys, UTC timestamps, correlation IDs, controlled configuration, and redaction before persistence.
Shared code must remain independent of application and adapter implementations.

acceptance: Runtime configuration rejects missing database settings, invalid concurrency or polling limits, weak bootstrap passwords, and empty workspace-root allowlists.
Secrets are read from deployment configuration and are never included in safe serialized configuration or normalized errors.
Redaction removes common authorization headers, cookies, access tokens, passwords, GitHub tokens, and credential-bearing URLs before persistence or display.
Stable typed identifiers and operation keys prevent accidental cross-entity key reuse while serializing cleanly across API boundaries.
API timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC values and correlation metadata can span HTTP, job, process, Git, GitHub, activity, and audit operations.
Shared contracts contain no imports from apps or concrete database, Git, GitHub, or process adapters.

test.description: Write runtime-config and redaction tests covering missing and unsafe configuration, bounds, safe serialization, token/cookie/URL redaction, false-positive preservation, operation-key stability, and UTC contract validation; verify the tests fail with no implementation.

implement.description: Implement schema-validated configuration and the shared contract, ID, time, error, correlation, idempotency, and redaction modules with a single public package entrypoint.

refactor.description: Consolidate duplicated validation and safe-serialization behavior, keep error codes stable and exhaustively typed, and rerun shared tests, typecheck, and lint.

verification: Run the shared package unit suite in isolation.
Run the redaction suite with representative gh, Git, process, cookie, and authorization output.
Verify the shared package dependency graph has no adapter or app dependencies.

requirements.description: Define and migrate the PostgreSQL core data model for the workspace, administrator, sessions, projects, releases, features, task approvals, and immutable pull-request identity.

patterns: PostgreSQL is the authoritative store and must encode project/release/feature ownership with foreign keys and uniqueness constraints.
Database tests must use isolated state or rollback transactions to avoid fixture conflicts and pollution.

acceptance: The schema contains one implicit workspace, one administrator account, revocable sessions, projects, releases, features, immutable task-approval snapshots, and pull-request identity records.
Foreign keys prevent a release, feature, task approval, or pull request from referencing entities in another project hierarchy.
Active projects enforce unique name, slug, GitHub repository identity, and canonical workspace path as required, while preserving archived history.
Releases enforce project-scoped name/version uniqueness and features enforce project-scoped slug uniqueness even though features belong through releases.
Pull-request repository, number, URL, head/base branches, and original identity are immutable separately from later mutable observations.
All persisted timestamps are timezone-aware UTC values and schema migrations apply and roll back cleanly in isolated database tests.

test.description: Add an isolated PostgreSQL integration suite that applies the core migration and proves hierarchy, uniqueness, archival, immutable approval/PR identity, and UTC constraints fail before the schema exists.

implement.description: Implement the typed PostgreSQL client, core schema and migration, transaction-aware fixtures, and minimal repositories needed to satisfy the core persistence tests.

refactor.description: Centralize IDs and timestamp mapping, remove repository query duplication, verify indexes support hierarchy lookups, and rerun migration and isolation tests.

verification: Apply migrations to a fresh PostgreSQL database and run the database package integration suite.
Run constraint tests in isolation and as a full suite to detect fixture pollution.
Inspect generated query plans for project/release/feature lookup indexes.

requirements.description: Extend PostgreSQL persistence with immutable development attempts, process ownership, progress, bounded logs, activity, audit, failure, worker, scheduling, idempotency, and outbox records.

patterns: The PRD requires durable jobs and reconciliation through PostgreSQL records, append-only audit/activity history, stable operation keys, and persisted external-effect intents.
Job/process records must carry project IDs so cross-project mismatch is visible and enforceable.

acceptance: Development attempts persist immutable feature, project, task approval, branch, enqueue, predecessor, process, heartbeat, exit, cancellation, and structured-result data with every required job status.
Database constraints prevent more than one claimed or running attempt per project and prevent duplicate active attempts for a stable approval or retry operation key.
Progress snapshots, diagnostic log chunks, failures, activity events, and audit events retain attempt and project ownership with append-only semantics.
Worker registrations, leases, scheduled reconciliation records, and outbox intents survive process restart and can be claimed transactionally.
Audit metadata supports actor, action, target, safe prior/next values, timestamp, correlation/job ID, and result without storing credential fields.
A transaction rollback leaves no partial domain mutation, job, activity, audit, idempotency, or outbox record.

test.description: Write isolated workflow-schema integration tests for immutable attempts, active-project uniqueness, stable idempotency, append-only events, lease/outbox claiming, cross-project foreign keys, and whole-transaction rollback; verify they fail before migration 0002.

implement.description: Add the workflow migration, typed schema, and transaction-scoped job, event, worker, and outbox repositories with database-enforced invariants.

refactor.description: Consolidate claim and append-only repository primitives, review partial indexes and lock ordering for races, and rerun the integration suite repeatedly to detect pollution.

verification: Race conflicting inserts and confirm the database admits only one active attempt per project.
Prove a failed transaction commits none of its feature, attempt, activity, audit, or outbox changes.
Re-run migration tests against fresh and already-migrated databases.

requirements.description: Implement the authoritative feature lifecycle state machine with exhaustive allowed, idempotent, forbidden, optimistic, and terminal transition behavior.

patterns: F-5 defines a closed state set and transition table with human, worker, GitHub adapter, poller, and deterministic guard owners.
Controllers and workers must request transitions through one deterministic domain service rather than updating feature state directly.

acceptance: Every state and every transition listed in F-5 is represented with its permitted trigger owner and cause.
An exhaustive matrix test accepts every allowed transition and rejects every unlisted source/target pair without changing state.
Repeating an already-applied transition with the same operation identity returns the prior result without emitting a second transition.
Expected prior state or row-version mismatch produces a typed conflict and no mutation.
Any eligible nonterminal state may enter BLOCKED only through the deterministic invariant guard, and DEVELOPMENT_MERGED rejects all outgoing transitions.
The transition result carries safe prior/next values, owner, cause, timestamp, and event metadata for transactional persistence.

test.description: Create an exhaustive state-transition matrix test first, including idempotent repeats, wrong owners, stale versions, BLOCKED guard entry, forbidden transitions, and terminal DEVELOPMENT_MERGED behavior; verify it fails with no state machine.

implement.description: Implement the closed state types, transition commands/results, and single deterministic state-machine service sufficient to satisfy the exhaustive matrix.

refactor.description: Generate transition lookup structures from one declarative table, enforce exhaustiveness at compile time, and rerun all matrix and mutation-safety tests.

verification: Run the state-machine unit suite and inspect its complete state-pair matrix.
Mutation-test representative allowed and forbidden rows to ensure the suite detects table changes.
Confirm no public API permits direct feature-state assignment.

requirements.description: Implement release development progress, lifecycle-derived attention, structured failure, and safe next-action domain policies.

patterns: Attention is derived from persisted workflow state rather than manually toggled flags.
Release progress counts DEVELOPMENT_MERGED among non-archived features and must never imply production release.

acceptance: Development progress is DEVELOPMENT_MERGED divided by non-archived features, handles zero features deterministically, and never labels a release released or production-ready.
Attention is produced for task review, development failed/interrupted, PR creation failed, CI failed, PR review, requested changes, BLOCKED, and stale GitHub synchronization.
Healthy waiting states, planned work, queued/running work, cancellation, completed handoff, and merged features do not produce attention.
Each attention result contains project, optional release, feature, reason, age basis, current state, category, and exactly one primary action.
Validation, queue, process, task-result, Git, GitHub, CI, cancellation, interruption, and stale-sync failures map to safe summaries and recommended next actions.
Raw credential-bearing adapter output cannot enter a failure or attention projection.

test.description: Write release-progress, complete state-by-state attention, stale-sync, and failure-mapping tests first, including empty/archived features and redacted actions; verify missing policies fail.

implement.description: Implement pure development-progress, attention-derivation, and failure-policy functions with stable reason and action codes.

refactor.description: Share exhaustive lifecycle classification data with the state machine where safe, remove duplicated labels, and rerun all domain tests and coverage.

verification: Run attention tests against every Phase 1 state.
Run release progress tests for empty, archived, mixed, and fully merged releases.
Verify UI-facing wording consistently says development progress and Development Merged.

requirements.description: Implement canonical workspace, safe relative task path, repository identity, and deterministic feature-branch value objects and validation.

patterns: Every user path must be resolved through realpath inside an operator allowlist and rechecked after joining relative input.
Feature branches use feature/<feature-id>-<slug> and safety code must reject destructive or ambiguous targets.

acceptance: Canonical project paths must exist, resolve by realpath beneath one configured root, and reject prefix tricks, root equality when disallowed, and symlink escapes.
Task paths reject absolute paths, empty paths, dot-dot traversal, non-JSON extensions, missing files, directories, and symlink escape after the project-relative join.
Repository identity normalizes configured GitHub owner/repository and supported remote URL forms without exposing embedded credentials.
Feature branch generation deterministically produces a valid feature/<feature-id>-<sanitized-slug> ref, rejects empty or unsafe output, and remains stable across retry.
Distinct feature IDs remain distinct even when titles sanitize to the same slug.
Property-based path and slug cases cannot escape roots or create invalid Git ref components.

test.description: Write temporary-directory and property-based tests for canonical roots, prefix collisions, traversal, symlink escape, task extension/existence, remote normalization, and Git branch sanitization before implementing the value objects.

implement.description: Implement the workspace/task path resolvers and repository/branch value objects using realpath and Git-ref-safe normalization with typed failures.

refactor.description: Centralize containment and normalization checks, remove stringly typed path/ref handling, and rerun tests on Unix path edge cases and randomized slugs.

verification: Run path tests against real symlinks and similarly prefixed directories.
Run git check-ref-format against generated branches.
Confirm normalized failures contain no credential-bearing remote URL.

requirements.description: Implement versioned autopilot task-file compatibility, semantic validation, exact approval snapshots, checksums, and tolerant atomic progress reads.

patterns: Current task files use a top-level requirements array and per-requirement acceptance, dependsOn, tdd test/implement/refactor pass flags, overall passes, stuck, blockedReason, invalidTest, and invalidTestReason fields.
Unknown compatible fields must round-trip in snapshots and task files must never be rewritten merely for display.

acceptance: Import validates the supported autopilot task schema and reports incompatible versions, missing required fields, duplicate requirement IDs, missing dependencies, dependency cycles, and impossible fresh/resumable states.
Known requirement fields normalize into structured progress while compatible unknown top-level and nested fields remain intact in the immutable approval snapshot.
Displaying or validating a task file does not rewrite its bytes, permissions, timestamps, or semantic content.
Approval stores the exact parsed requirements, source-byte checksum, schema compatibility version, and safe relative path while leaving the mutable source file in place.

Atomic replacement reads never accept partial JSON; a malformed transient update retains the last valid snapshot and yields a diagnostic until bounded retry or terminal process evidence makes it unrecoverable.
Parsed summaries expose goals, non-goals, dependencies, acceptance, Red/Green/Refactor status, pass/stuck/invalid counts, blocked reasons, and whether all requirements truly pass.

test.description: Create task artifact tests from the installed schema and fixtures, adding cases for duplicate/missing/cyclic dependencies, unknown-field preservation, exact checksums, no-rewrite display, atomic replacement, partial JSON, fresh/resumable semantics, and all-pass evaluation; verify they fail first.

implement.description: Implement versioned schemas, semantic graph validation, read-only parsing, immutable snapshot/checksum creation, normalized summaries, and bounded tolerant reads.

refactor.description: Separate wire-schema preservation from normalized views, reuse one dependency graph traversal, and rerun compatibility fixtures plus randomized atomic-read tests.

verification: Validate all installed autopilot-multi task fixtures and intentional invalid variants.
Compare task file hashes before and after validation/display operations.
Simulate concurrent atomic replacement and partial writes with a fake clock and bounded retries.

requirements.description: Define AutopilotRunner and implement the current global autopilotagent CLI adapter with contract-tested spawning, liveness, process identity, structured result normalization, and branch compatibility.

patterns: The wrapper is invoked as autopilotagent <validated-task-path>, stores run.pid beside the task file, mutates task state, emits notes/analytics, and accepts SIGUSR1.
The current slash command checks out a branch derived from the task basename, which requires an explicit, tested compatibility strategy for Console's deterministic branch contract.

acceptance: AutopilotRunner covers runtime/task validation, direct start, verified identity, liveness, structured progress/result reads, notes/analytics summaries, relevant commits, graceful/forced signaling hooks, and normalized redacted outcomes.

The CLI adapter spawns the fixed autopilotagent executable with an argument array containing only the validated relative task path, the canonical project cwd, a minimal allowlisted environment, and shell disabled.
The adapter records wrapper PID plus OS start identity and verifies project, feature, and process identity before every liveness or signal operation.
Contract tests pin the current sibling run.pid, mutable task, notes, analytics, exit, SIGUSR1, and no-interactive-shell behavior without requiring the real CLI in the default suite.

A documented compatibility strategy proves current task-basename checkout behavior cannot divert commits or pushes away from the persisted feature/<feature-id>-<slug> branch, and it uses no engine fork, force push, history rewrite, branch deletion, or task-file rewrite.
The opt-in installed-CLI suite reports a clear compatibility failure when current autopilot-multi behavior changes and never runs in ordinary CI by default.
Captured stdout and stderr are diagnostic only, bounded upstream, redacted before return, and never interpreted as workflow commands.

test.description: Build a controllable fake executable and failing adapter integration tests for argv/cwd/env/shell, PID start identity, liveness, task/notes/analytics results, exit mapping, redaction, and deterministic-branch compatibility; add an opt-in contract test against the installed CLI.

implement.description: Implement the AutopilotRunner interface, direct CLI adapter, process identity checks, normalized results, and the tested non-destructive compatibility strategy documented in docs/architecture/autopilot-cli-compatibility.md.

refactor.description: Isolate OS process inspection behind injectable ports, minimize the child environment, centralize redaction/result mapping, and rerun fake plus opt-in contract suites.

verification: Run the fake executable suite for success, nonzero exit, hang, malformed progress, and branch-switch behavior.
Run the installed-CLI contract suite explicitly in a disposable fixture repository.
Inspect spawned process arguments and environment and confirm no shell or arbitrary command template is accepted.

requirements.description: Implement constrained Git repository validation, preflight, deterministic branch creation/reuse, commit observation, and idempotent safe push operations.

patterns: Git operations are deterministic adapter behavior and must validate real path, repository identity, remote, base, task path, and generated branch.
Phase 1 forbids force push, history rewrite, destructive reset, branch deletion, and discarding workspace changes.

acceptance: Registration and run preflight verify canonical path, Git worktree, normalized configured remote, repository identity, development branch, task artifact, and expected feature branch.
The first attempt fetches the configured remote and creates feature/<feature-id>-<slug> from the current remote development branch; retry reuses the same branch and task progress.
Unrelated staged, unstaged, or untracked changes reject execution while the selected approved task artifact may be present or modified according to an explicit allow rule.
Repository, base, remote, task checksum, path, or branch mismatch returns a safe actionable error before Autopilot starts.
Push publishes the verified current feature HEAD to the one persisted remote feature branch and repeated push intents remain idempotent.
The adapter exposes no force-push, reset-hard, clean, history rewrite, branch-delete, or arbitrary Git command operation.
Relevant commit observation is bounded to the verified feature branch and records immutable hashes without trusting commit text as commands.

test.description: Create temporary-repository integration tests for remote/base fetch, first branch creation, retry reuse, task-only dirtiness, unrelated dirtiness, repository/remote/base mismatch, branch compatibility, commit observation, safe push idempotency, and forbidden destructive operations; verify failures first.

implement.description: Implement the narrow GitGateway, CLI command runner with fixed subcommands/argv, preflight policy, deterministic branch workflow, commit observer, and safe idempotent push.

refactor.description: Centralize repository assertions before all effects, remove any generic command escape hatch, normalize redacted errors, and rerun temp-repository tests under retry scenarios.

verification: Run the full Git integration suite using only disposable local remotes.
Search the public adapter API for destructive Git verbs or arbitrary command parameters.
Verify repeat preflight and push operations preserve branch and history.

requirements.description: Define GitHubGateway and implement a typed gh CLI adapter for validation, idempotent PR lookup/creation, and normalized current-head status observations.

patterns: gh must be invoked behind a typed boundary using requested JSON fields; domain code must not parse human-formatted output.
PR identity is immutable while head SHA, checks, review decision, open/closed/merged state, merge commit, and timestamps are observations.

acceptance: Gateway validation covers gh authentication, repository read access, configured remote identity, and a non-mutating push-permission check where feasible.
Existing PR lookup uses repository plus exact head/base branch and distinguishes open, closed, and merged matches before creation.
PR creation requests and validates JSON fields and returns immutable repository, number, URL, original head SHA, head branch, and base branch identity.
Status reads normalize current head SHA, checks for that SHA only, review decision, open/closed/merged state, merge commit, and relevant timestamps.
Malformed or human-formatted gh output is rejected with a normalized redacted adapter error rather than parsed ad hoc.
No gateway operation approves or merges a pull request.

test.description: Create a fake gh boundary and failing tests for auth/repository validation, existing PR lookup, creation, malformed JSON, head changes, pending/passing/failing current-head checks, requested changes, close, merge, redaction, and absence of merge operations.

implement.description: Implement the typed GitHubGateway, fixed gh argv commands requesting explicit JSON fields, response schemas, and normalized status/error mapping.

refactor.description: Deduplicate gh execution and schema validation, make status mapping exhaustive and current-head-aware, and rerun adapter tests with credential-bearing error fixtures.

verification: Run the gateway unit suite with all fake gh response variants.
Inspect command fixtures and confirm every status command requests machine-readable JSON.
Search the gateway API and implementation to confirm no approve or merge operation exists.

requirements.description: Implement single-administrator bootstrap authentication, opaque revocable PostgreSQL sessions, secure cookies, rate limiting, and CSRF protection.

patterns: Phase 1 has exactly one administrator bootstrapped from secret deployment configuration.
Sessions use opaque revocable values in HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies and state-changing browser requests require CSRF defense.

acceptance: Startup creates at most one administrator from a strength-validated deployment password and stores only a current password hash, never plaintext.
Successful login rotates to a cryptographically random opaque session token while PostgreSQL stores only a verifier or hash sufficient for revocation.
Session cookies are HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, use a constrained path, and enable Secure in production.
Expiration, logout, password/bootstrap rotation as defined, and explicit revocation make the server-side session unusable immediately.
Login attempts are rate-limited without leaking whether credentials partially matched.
Every state-changing browser request must present valid same-origin/CSRF evidence in addition to the session cookie, while login and documented health checks remain available as specified.
Passwords, raw session tokens, cookies, and authentication headers never enter application logs, audit metadata, or returned errors.

test.description: Write database-backed authentication tests first for one-admin bootstrap, weak password rejection, hash-only storage, login success/failure, opaque token storage, cookie flags, expiration/revocation/logout, rate limits with fake time, CSRF acceptance/rejection, and redaction.

implement.description: Implement password bootstrap/hashing, session lifecycle, secure cookie construction, rate limiting, and CSRF services against transaction-scoped database repositories.

refactor.description: Centralize secret-safe comparisons and time injection, remove duplicated session queries, and rerun authentication tests in isolation and full-suite order.

verification: Run authentication integration tests with isolated database state and fake time.
Inspect database rows and logs to confirm no plaintext password or raw token is persisted.
Verify production and development cookie attributes separately.

requirements.description: Implement transactional project registration, integration validation, protected configuration changes, and archival with audit history.

patterns: Projects register existing repositories only after path, Git, remote, branch, Autopilot, gh auth, and GitHub access checks all succeed.
Mutation and audit records should commit together and project history is archived, not destructively deleted.

acceptance: Validation returns one safe structured result for canonical root containment, Git repository, remote identity, development branch, autopilotagent availability/task compatibility, gh authentication, repository access, and push feasibility.
A project is saved only when every required validation passes and its canonical path, name, slug, and repository identity satisfy active uniqueness constraints.
Validation output reports each check without exposing credentials or unrestricted command output.
Queued or active jobs prevent path, repository, development-branch changes and prevent archival.
Archival preserves releases, features, jobs, pull requests, activity, and audit history and never deletes the checkout.
Create, validation, update, rejection, and archive outcomes append structured audit events transactionally with the mutation where applicable.

test.description: Write transaction-backed project service tests with fake Git, GitHub, and Autopilot adapters for every validation failure, successful save, uniqueness, protected active-job edits, archival, redaction, and audit rollback; verify they fail before the service.

implement.description: Implement project entities, validation orchestration, transactional create/update/archive commands, repository operations, and audit emission using the existing narrow adapters.

refactor.description: Make validation checks independently testable while preserving one aggregate result, consolidate protected-field policy, and rerun rollback plus adapter-error cases.

verification: Run project service tests with each adapter failure injected independently.
Attempt duplicate canonical paths through symlink aliases and confirm rejection.
Confirm archival leaves all historical foreign-key records queryable.

requirements.description: Implement transactional release and feature planning, project-scoped uniqueness, deterministic branches, archival guards, development status, and audit events.

patterns: Releases belong to one project and features belong to one release while feature slugs remain project-scoped.
New features begin PLANNED and release status/progress reflects development only.

test.description: Write release/feature integration tests first for creation, ordering, project-scoped uniqueness, cross-project rejection, PLANNED defaults, deterministic branches, development status/progress, archive guards, activity/audit atomicity, and rollback.

implement.description: Implement release and feature entities/services plus repository queries and transactional event/audit writes required by the tests.

refactor.description: Share project ownership guards and mutation transaction helpers, keep release calculations pure, and rerun isolated and combined service suites.

acceptance: A project can create ordered releases with project-unique name/version, optional description, Planned/In Development/Development Merged status, and UTC timestamps.
A release can create features with project-scoped unique slug, title, optional summary, PLANNED state, deterministic generated branch, and no task/job/PR references.
Cross-project release/feature association is rejected both by domain policy and database constraints.
Release development status and progress derive from non-archived feature states and use development-only wording.
A release with any queued or active feature job cannot be archived; allowed archival retains history.
Every create, validation rejection, update, and archive mutation records an append-only audit and structured activity event in the same transaction.
verification: Create two projects with colliding release and feature slugs and verify only project-scoped collisions are rejected.
Exercise archive guards with queued and active attempts.
Compare persisted activity/audit records with every successful mutation.

requirements.description: Implement safe task attachment, immutable approval invalidation/reapproval, and atomic idempotent Approve & Queue Development.

patterns: Attaching valid tasks moves PLANNED to TASKS_REVIEW; approval of the displayed checksum and first queue creation are one human transaction.
Source task files remain mutable in the project while every approved snapshot/checksum remains immutable and audited.

acceptance: Only a safe valid project-relative task JSON can attach, and the feature enters TASKS_REVIEW through the state machine with a structured activity/audit record.
Approval rejects a stale displayed checksum, snapshots the exact current approved artifact, identifies the administrator actor, and never mutates the source task file.

Approve & Queue Development changes TASKS_REVIEW to QUEUED and creates exactly one immutable initial attempt atomically; any failure rolls back approval, transition, attempt, activity, audit, and idempotency state.
Repeated submissions with the same stable operation key return the same attempt and create no duplicate transition, event, or job.
Task replacement is allowed before approval or after failed/interrupted/cancelled attempts only when prior approval is explicitly invalidated, and replacement/reapproval are audited.
Task replacement, approval, or queueing is rejected in every other lifecycle state.

test.description: Write isolated database integration tests first for attach, stale checksum, exact snapshot, no source rewrite, approval-and-enqueue rollback, duplicate operation keys, legal replacement/invalidation/reapproval, illegal lifecycle states, and audit/activity consistency.

implement.description: Implement transactional task artifact and approval services that compose path/task validation, state transitions, immutable snapshots, idempotency, attempt creation, activity, and audit repositories.

refactor.description: Extract one approval transaction boundary and one replacement policy, remove duplicate checksum reads, and rerun race plus rollback tests repeatedly.

verification: Race duplicate approval requests and confirm one approval and one attempt persist.
Inject failures after each transaction step and confirm total rollback.
Verify the approved snapshot remains unchanged after the source task file is mutated.

requirements.description: Implement PostgreSQL FIFO queue claiming, configurable global capacity, per-project mutual exclusion, worker leases, heartbeats, and interruption reconciliation.

patterns: Queue claims use transactional PostgreSQL row locking with skip-locked semantics and database-enforced active-project uniqueness.
Expired ownership becomes INTERRUPTED and is never automatically requeued or relaunched.

acceptance: Eligible attempts are claimed oldest approval/enqueue first using one transaction and are claimed at most once when multiple worker processes race.
The configured global active limit defaults to four: four different projects may run, a fifth stays queued, and capacity is configurable to valid positive bounds.
Two attempts for the same project never become active concurrently even when workers race and global capacity remains.
A successful claim records worker, lease, start, heartbeat, RUNNING job status, DEVELOPING feature transition, activity, and audit atomically.
Heartbeats renew only matching live ownership; stale workers cannot overwrite a newer owner.
Expired leases become job INTERRUPTED and feature DEVELOPMENT_INTERRUPTED with events, but no new attempt is enqueued and no process is launched automatically.
Queue timing tests use fake clocks and synchronization barriers, never arbitrary sleeps.

test.description: Write database race tests first for FIFO eligibility, duplicate claims, four-job global capacity, same-project exclusion, claim transaction rollback, heartbeat ownership, and expired-lease interruption without requeue using barriers and fake time.

implement.description: Implement transactional skip-locked queue claims, capacity/project guards, leases, heartbeats, and reconciliation using job, state transition, activity, and audit repositories.

requirements.description: Implement the durable development worker orchestration from claim through Git preflight, Autopilot execution, heartbeat, deterministic result verification, and development completion or failure.

patterns: The API only enqueues; a separate server-side worker owns long-running execution and persists identity and heartbeat independent of browsers.
A zero process exit is successful only when every structured requirement passes and none is stuck or invalid.

acceptance: A registered worker claims durable attempts and performs fresh/retry Git, project, task-checksum, branch, process, and adapter preflight before spawning anything.
The worker persists verified process identity, heartbeat, and ownership before treating the attempt as running and continues without an initiating HTTP or browser connection.
The first attempt creates the deterministic branch from the remote development branch; retry uses persisted branch and current structured task progress.
Successful exit plus every requirement passes transitions job to SUCCEEDED and feature to DEVELOPMENT_COMPLETE with structured result, activity, audit, and a persisted PR-handoff intent.

Nonzero exit, timeout, stuck, invalidTest, unresolved or unpassed requirement, malformed terminal task state, or preflight failure produces the correct safe FAILED/BLOCKED result and never creates a PR intent when unsafe.
Worker restart never assumes ownership of an unverified existing process and no worker can act on a job from another project.

test.description: Write worker integration tests first with fake queue, Git, clock, and Autopilot adapters for claim/preflight/spawn ordering, persisted identity/heartbeat, browser/API independence, all-pass success, zero-exit-unpassed failure, nonzero/stuck/invalid/malformed outcomes, project mismatch, and PR-intent gating.

implement.description: Implement worker registration, claim loop, preflight orchestration, direct Autopilot start, heartbeat lifecycle, result verification, and transactional completion/failure effects.

refactor.description: Separate pure result classification from effect orchestration, make clocks and adapters injectable, minimize transaction duration around external effects, and rerun crash-boundary cases.

verification: Run development worker tests with a controllable fake executable.
Terminate the API test process after enqueue and confirm the worker finishes from persisted state.
Verify no PR intent exists for any non-passing structured task result.

requirements.description: Persist structured requirement progress, task-change snapshots, notes/analytics/commit summaries, bounded diagnostic logs, and paginated activity independently of live connections.

patterns: Structured task JSON, notes, analytics, and Git history are primary evidence; terminal output remains bounded diagnostics only.
Every live view must reconstruct from persisted REST state after disconnect and SSE is never authoritative.

acceptance: Task snapshots persist whenever a valid file change is observed and periodically during active work, with monotonic source version and last-valid preservation.
Snapshots expose total, passed, active, stuck, invalid, remaining, dependency state, acceptance, TDD Red/Green/Refactor phases, blocked reasons, and last update time.
Meaningful task, notes, analytics, and relevant commit changes produce typed requirement/TDD/commit/job activity events without interpreting arbitrary text as commands.
Diagnostic stdout/stderr is redacted before storage, bounded by a configurable per-attempt cap, ordered, and terminated with an explicit truncation marker without removing structured evidence.
Malformed concurrent task writes retain the last valid snapshot, append a diagnostic event, and fail only according to bounded retry or terminal-result policy.
Global and project activity queries are newest-first, cursor-paginated, and rebuild the same state after observer, worker, API, or browser restart.

test.description: Write progress observer integration tests first for atomic and malformed updates, periodic snapshots with fake time, monotonic ordering, phase/activity derivation, notes/analytics/commit ingestion, redacted bounded logs, truncation, pagination, and restart reconstruction.

implement.description: Implement persisted progress observation, activity projection, notes/analytics parsing, relevant commit ingestion, and bounded redacted diagnostic storage wired into development execution.

verification: Update a task fixture atomically and partially while a fake job runs and inspect snapshot history.
Exceed the log cap and verify one redacted truncation marker plus intact structured progress.
Restart observer and query layers and compare reconstructed summaries and pagination.

requirements.description: Implement queued/running cancellation, verified process-tree escalation, orphan interruption handling, and explicit immutable retry on the existing branch.

patterns: Cancellation signals the verified wrapper PID with SIGUSR1, waits a bounded grace period, then escalates to SIGTERM and SIGKILL for the captured process tree.
Interruption and cancellation preserve evidence; retry is always explicit and creates a distinct attempt.

acceptance: Cancelling QUEUED atomically produces CANCELLED/DEVELOPMENT_CANCELLED without spawning a process; cancelling RUNNING first persists CANCEL_REQUESTED and metadata.

Running cancellation verifies recorded PID start identity, feature, project, and process tree before SIGUSR1, waits configurable fake-clock grace, then uses bounded SIGTERM and SIGKILL only for verified survivors.
PID reuse, identity mismatch, or unrelated descendants are never signaled and instead create a safe actionable interruption or BLOCKED failure.
Worker restart/lost ownership attempts verified orphan cleanup, marks job INTERRUPTED and feature DEVELOPMENT_INTERRUPTED once, and never automatically resumes or relaunches.
Retry is available only for failed/interrupted/cancelled attempts after liveness verification proves no associated process remains.
Retry creates a new immutable linked attempt using the same feature branch and current structured task progress while retaining all prior attempts, logs, events, and results.
Duplicate cancel and retry operation keys remain idempotent.

test.description: Use a fake process tree and fake clock to write failing tests for queued cancellation, SIGUSR1/TERM/KILL escalation, graceful exit, descendants, PID reuse/mismatch, orphan cleanup, interruption without relaunch, retry liveness refusal, immutable linked attempts, same-branch resume, and duplicate operations.

implement.description: Implement verified process-tree inspection, cancellation controller, orphan reconciler, and transactional retry service using AutopilotRunner and persisted identity/attempt data.

refactor.description: Unify liveness and identity predicates across cancellation/reconciliation/retry, remove real-time sleeps from tests and orchestration, and rerun escalation cases repeatedly.

verification: Run process tests with a controllable executable that ignores selected signals.
Simulate PID reuse and confirm no signal is sent.
Retry after verified exit and confirm a new attempt points to the prior attempt and same branch.

requirements.description: Implement persisted Git/PR handoff, exactly-once PR identity, durable current-head CI/review polling, backoff, stale-observation protection, and external merge detection.

patterns: External effects use persisted intent and reconciliation so crashes between database, push, and GitHub calls cannot duplicate PRs.
Polling is durable, current-head-aware, monotonic, and never depends on an open browser.

acceptance: A DEVELOPMENT_COMPLETE feature transitions to PR_CREATING, verifies and pushes its branch, checks persisted and GitHub PR identity, and stores exactly one existing or newly created PR before CI_RUNNING.
Concurrent/retried handoff and crashes before or after push/create cannot produce a second PR for the repository/head branch.
A bounded push or PR creation failure transitions to PR_CREATION_FAILED with attention and requires explicit retry; successful retry reuses persisted intent and existing external effects.
A durable scheduled worker polls open Phase 1 PRs at least once per configured minute and reconciles head SHA, current-head checks, review decision, PR state, merge commit, and timestamps.

Pending checks map to CI_RUNNING, failed current-head checks to CI_FAILED, all passing or valid no-check cases to PR_REVIEW, and requested changes to PR_CHANGES_REQUESTED with allowed recovery transitions.

A newer head or observation is never overwritten by an older poll; transient errors back off without state regression, and repeated failures create stale-sync attention while preserving last known state.
Merged-to-configured-base moves to terminal DEVELOPMENT_MERGED and updates activity/audit/progress; closed without merge enters BLOCKED; no code path approves or merges a PR.

test.description: Write integration tests first with fake Git/GitHub and persisted outbox/scheduler state for crash boundaries, concurrent PR creation, existing PR reuse, push/create retry, head changes, pending/pass/fail/no checks, requested changes, stale poll ordering, backoff, closed-without-merge, and merge detection.

verification: Race and crash handoff at each external-effect boundary and confirm one PR identity.

requirements.description: Enforce the authenticated HTTP boundary, session lifecycle, CSRF/origin validation, safe error envelopes, and request correlation for every registered API route.

patterns: Public access uses an exact method-and-path allowlist.
Authenticated browser mutations require session, CSRF, and trusted-origin evidence.
Errors and logs are normalized and redacted before exposure.

acceptance: Only login and redacted liveness/readiness endpoints are public; every other registered route rejects missing, invalid, expired, and revoked sessions.
Every browser mutation rejects missing or invalid CSRF evidence and rejects an untrusted Origin before executing a domain mutation.
Login and logout use opaque revocable sessions and safe cookies without returning or logging raw session tokens.
Every response carries a correlation ID, and production errors use a typed redacted envelope without stack traces or credentials.

Readiness separately reports database access, a fresh worker heartbeat with capacity and active-job counts, and Autopilot runtime availability.

requirements.description: Provide validated and ownership-safe project, release, and feature mutation APIs.

patterns: Strict request schemas feed project-scoped domain services.
Protected edits and archival are rejected while queued or active work exists.

Authenticated APIs create, update, order, and archive project-owned releases while rejecting cross-project references and active-work conflicts.
Authenticated APIs create and update project-owned features with project-scoped slugs, deterministic branch context, and lifecycle guards.
Invalid, stale, cross-project, or unsafe requests return stable redacted errors and leave no partial database mutation.

requirements.description: Provide the complete task-artifact attach, review, approve, invalidate, remove, replace, and reapprove API lifecycle.

patterns: Task paths are project-relative and resolved through the shared path-security boundary.
Approval stores an immutable snapshot and checksum while preserving prior attempts.

acceptance: Attach rejects absolute paths, traversal, symlink escape, schema errors, semantic errors, and task files that are neither fresh nor resumable.
Review returns structured goals, non-goals, requirements, dependencies, acceptance, TDD phases, pass/stuck/invalid state, and blocked reasons.
Approve requires the displayed checksum and exact project/feature confirmation and atomically stores approval plus one queued attempt.
Remove, invalidate, replace, and reapprove are exposed only in legal lifecycle states and preserve prior approval and attempt history.

requirements.description: Make approve, cancel, development retry, and PR retry HTTP operations durable, promptly returning, and idempotent without executing worker-owned effects in request scope.

patterns: The API persists an operation result or worker intent before returning.

acceptance: Approve, cancel, development retry, and PR retry require stable operation keys plus exact project/feature confirmation where process-affecting.
Concurrent or repeated requests with the same operation key return the original outcome and create no duplicate attempt, intent, activity, or audit event.
Queue and action endpoints return within two seconds at target fixture scale and never wait for process signaling, worker claim, Git, or GitHub completion.
API handlers persist worker-owned commands and do not invoke Autopilot, process-tree, Git, or GitHub effects directly.

requirements.description: Compose worker-owned running cancellation, cancellation escalation, safe retry, and orphan reconciliation end to end.

Only current-head observations update CI/review state; stale observations never overwrite newer head or state.
External merge and closed-without-merge are persisted with the specified feature transition, attention, activity, and audit behavior.

Apply out-of-order GitHub observations and confirm state monotonicity.

requirements.description: Provide a production Compose stack with isolated services, explicit workspace mounts, durable storage, secret configuration, dependency health checks, and validated worker tools.

patterns: PostgreSQL, migration, API, worker, and web are separate services.
Only the worker receives writable allowlisted project mounts.

acceptance: Compose starts PostgreSQL, one-shot migrations, API, worker, and web with dependency conditions that use service health or successful completion.
PostgreSQL data and bounded diagnostics use persistent volumes; credentials and authentication values come from required environment/secret configuration and are absent from images and examples.
Only explicitly configured allowlisted project paths are writable in the worker; API access is read-only if needed and web receives no project mount.
The worker image contains or startup-validates autopilotagent, the configured agent CLI, git, jq, and gh.
PostgreSQL, API, worker, and web have meaningful health checks, and dependent services wait for the health they require.

test.description: Extend Compose contract tests to assert worker health, dependency conditions, mount permissions, required secrets, persistent volumes, and tool validation.

implement.description: Add worker health and finish Compose/image isolation, secret, volume, and tool-validation wiring.

Build every image and start the complete stack from empty volumes.
Inspect mounts and environment inside each service and run every health check.

requirements.description: Wire production observability and provide operator documentation that matches the actual runtime.

patterns: Observability primitives redact before emission and use bounded storage.
Operator docs state implemented behavior and explicit limitations without claiming uncomposed flows.

acceptance: Structured logs include correlation, project, feature, attempt/job, adapter, and worker context where applicable after redaction.
Runtime metrics are updated from real operations for queue depth, active jobs, oldest queued age, heartbeat age, durations, interruptions, Git/GitHub errors, polling lag, and attention counts.
Diagnostic retention enforces documented per-attempt and total limits with explicit truncation while preserving structured progress and audit data.
Deployment docs cover prerequisites, Bun/autopilotagent initialization, mounts, secrets, migrations, trusted TLS proxy, Secure cookies, startup, and health.
Operations docs cover backup, restore, cancellation/escalation, interruption, retry, GitHub reconciliation, diagnostics, retention, and safe upgrades exactly as production composition behaves.

test.description: Add production-composition tests that drive real runtime events and assert every required log/metric/retention value plus documentation contract checks for all operator procedures.

refactor.description: Centralize instrumentation boundaries and remove documentation claims that cannot be traced to production code.

verification: Run a queued, successful, failed, interrupted, cancelled, Git-error, and GitHub-error flow and inspect metrics/logs.
Force diagnostic limits and confirm bounded storage plus truncation markers.
Execute deployment and recovery documentation against a fresh Compose stack.

requirements.description: Prove the complete owner journey through production-equivalent API and worker composition using fake external executables and adapters.

patterns: The test uses real PostgreSQL and production-equivalent composition with fake process/Git/GitHub boundaries.
The journey advances through public API commands and durable worker consumers rather than fixture-only helper shortcuts.

acceptance: An unauthenticated visitor sees no portfolio data or mutations; the sole administrator logs in and out through revocable secure sessions.

One test completes register project, validate, create release/feature, attach/review/approve, queue, worker development, branch push, one PR, current-head CI running/pass, review, external merge, and merge detection.
The test uses the same durable command consumers and production worker supervisor as runtime composition, substituting only controlled external adapters/executables.
Final feature, release, attempt, PR, overview, attention, activity, and audit state exactly reconstructs every meaningful transition and actor.
The test asserts Console exposes no PR approve or merge action.

test.description: Replace fixture-only runDevelopmentOnce/runPrHandoff shortcuts with a production-equivalent supervisor test covering the complete CI and review sequence plus exact state/event/audit assertions.

Compare final activity and audit sequences with every expected transition and actor.

requirements.description: Prove browser, API, and worker restart durability with actual component replacement and persisted ownership policy.

patterns: A restart test disposes and recreates the component under test against the same database.
Running ownership is either preserved by a live worker or becomes safely interrupted; it is never silently relaunched.

acceptance: Closing and recreating a browser/session leaves queued and running work unchanged and reconstructable from persisted APIs.
Stopping and recreating the API process while a worker runs does not stop or duplicate the attempt.
Stopping and recreating a worker applies lease/process policy: live owned work remains singular or expired ownership becomes INTERRUPTED with evidence and no automatic retry.
Restart during Git push, PR creation, or GitHub polling reconciles to one external effect and monotonic state.
Every restart assertion is unconditional and waits on bounded state transitions rather than accepting multiple unrelated outcomes.

test.description: Rewrite durability tests to dispose/recreate browser, API, and worker components and restart at development, cancellation, push, PR-create, and poll boundaries.

implement.description: Add restartable test composition and fix any ownership or persisted-intent gaps exposed by real component replacement.

refactor.description: Centralize bounded state waiters and component lifecycle helpers; remove simulated restart comments and conditional assertions.

verification: Demonstrate the API and worker objects/processes are actually disposed and recreated.
Repeat every restart boundary and confirm one attempt, process, push, and PR.
Search the suite for conditional success assertions or multi-state allowances.

requirements.description: Prove runtime concurrency, same-project exclusion, operation idempotency, and stale-observation protection through real queue and worker behavior.

patterns: Concurrency proof drives queue claims and controllable worker runs instead of assigning RUNNING through direct SQL.
Idempotency is asserted by both returned outcome and durable row/event counts.

acceptance: Four controllable attempts from four projects run simultaneously and a fifth remains queued until a slot opens.
Two attempts for one project never own overlapping worker processes under a real claim race.
Duplicate approvals, cancellations, development retries, pushes, and PR creates each return one durable outcome with one corresponding effect.
Concurrent different operation keys obey lifecycle rules without partial or duplicate state.
Stale feature versions, task checksums, process observations, and GitHub poll observations cannot overwrite newer state.

test.description: Replace direct-SQL RUNNING simulation with controllable production worker claims and add the fifth-waits, duplicate-effect, and stale-observation cases.

implement.description: Fix runtime supervision, durable operation uniqueness, and monotonic writes exposed by the real concurrency tests.

refactor.description: Use reusable barriers and bounded events for deterministic races without sleeps.

verification: Observe four live controllable processes and a queued fifth.
Race every idempotent operation and count attempts, intents, activities, audits, pushes, and PRs.
Replay stale versions and observations after newer writes.

requirements.description: Prove the complete Phase 1 security boundary with exact failures and no conditionally skipped assertions.

patterns: Security tests assert exact stable error codes and prove no mutation/effect occurred.
Every fixture setup must succeed before testing the intended boundary; setup failure is never treated as acceptable security behavior.

acceptance: Exact tests reject workspace traversal, symlink escape, absolute/traversing task paths, repository mismatch, and unrelated dirty worktrees without mutation.
Exact tests prevent duplicate process and duplicate PR identity and refuse signaling on PID reuse.
Credential redaction covers headers, cookies, URLs, tokens, nested values, logs, errors, activity, audit, and health.
Missing/invalid CSRF or Origin, missing/expired/revoked session, and cross-project mutation return the documented status/code and no mutation.
A genuine stale row version, stale checksum, stale process observation, and stale GitHub poll each fail to overwrite newer state.
No test hides its assertion behind conditional setup success or accepts unrelated status codes.

test.description: Rewrite the security matrix with mandatory successful setup, exact status/error codes, no-mutation/effect assertions, and all path/Git/process/PR/session/CSRF/staleness cases.

requirements.description: Prove portfolio and feature-detail read performance at the documented Phase 1 scale.

patterns: The supported profile uses real PostgreSQL with deterministic seed size and measured warm reads.
The assertion reports sample count and p95 rather than only extending test timeout.

acceptance: The fixture contains exactly 10 projects, 100 releases, 500 non-archived features, and four active jobs.
At least 95 percent of authenticated Overview reads complete in under one second on the documented supported single-server profile.
At least 95 percent of authenticated feature-detail reads complete in under one second on the same profile.
The test records sample count, warm-up policy, p95 values, database profile, and failure diagnostics without using a longer test timeout as the performance assertion.

requirements.description: Prove every primary owner journey at desktop and 375x667 with real keyboard operation and automated WCAG 2.2 AA checks.

patterns: A journey test completes the mutation and verifies its result; opening a page or dialog is not completion.
Accessibility uses a standards-based engine plus explicit keyboard, focus, contrast, and live-region assertions.

acceptance: Login, portfolio review, project registration, release/feature creation, task attach/review/approval, progress, cancellation, retry, failure, and PR-link journeys complete at 375x667 without page-level horizontal scrolling.
Keyboard-only tests complete every primary desktop workflow with logical order, visible focus, dialog focus placement/restoration, and no focus trap.
A standards-based automated accessibility scan reports no serious WCAG 2.2 AA violations on every core screen and includes color-contrast rules.
Primary tap targets are at least 44x44 where practical and no critical action requires hover, right-click, drag, or desktop-only interaction.
The browser suite asserts no Console PR approve or merge action.

Review the accessibility scanner output for every core route.

requirements.description: Enforce at least 90 percent branch coverage independently for every named critical module.

patterns: Coverage is checked per critical module, so highly covered files cannot mask an uncovered module.
Database-backed and process-backed branches run in the default critical coverage command.

acceptance: The gate lists each critical domain, queue, path-security, process-control, Git, GitHub, and Autopilot adapter module explicitly.
Every listed module reports at least 90 percent branch coverage; aggregate package coverage cannot substitute for a low module.
The coverage command provisions or documents its required PostgreSQL/process fixtures and returns nonzero when any required suite cannot execute.
No skipped or conditionally disabled critical test contributes to a passing coverage gate.

requirements.description: Provide one reproducible Phase 1 release-qualification command that passes every required code, database, process, browser, migration, image, and deployment gate without skipped critical tests.

patterns: Release qualification is a gate that depends on feature requirements; it does not duplicate them.
The command fails closed when PostgreSQL, process tools, browser binaries, Docker, migrations, or critical contracts are unavailable.

acceptance: One documented command runs workspace typecheck, lint, unit tests, database integration tests, process/Git/API tests, browser E2E, critical coverage, production builds, migrations, image builds, Compose validation, and deployment smoke checks.
The command provisions or verifies every required dependency and fails with an actionable message instead of silently skipping a gate.
No critical installed-CLI, database, process, browser, migration, image, or deployment test is skipped or opt-in when Phase 1 qualification is claimed.
The command succeeds twice consecutively from a clean documented environment with no detected flake.
The requirement ledger, README, deployment guide, operations guide, and changelog report the same qualification status.
